gaps.sentence: He went back inside, ___ the danger.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the danger' — noun phrase; although needs a clause.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: ___ the price, the location is absolutely perfect.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from the price' = the only negative in an otherwise positive description.

gaps.sentence: Sales fell sharply last quarter; ___, the board cut the dividend.
gaps.explanation: The fall in sales caused the cut: as a result marks the consequence.

gaps.sentence: She is not only a gifted violinist ___ a composer of some note.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only A but also B' joins the two parallel noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: ___ her age, she still runs marathons.
gaps.explanation: 'In spite of' + noun (her age); the conjunctions would need a clause.

gaps.sentence: ___ most thrillers, the film reveals the killer in the opening scene.
gaps.explanation: 'Unlike + noun phrase' marks difference from a general category.

gaps.sentence: ___ the theory is elegant, the data simply don't support it.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' grants the fact (the theory is elegant) before contradicting it.
